column1: # Functions where fcheck says DIFFERS and the C is not the cause (tools/fcheck_gate.py turns that into "unchecked" with the reason).
# name<TAB>reason. Only for a difference shown to come from the harness or from the host having no hardware to act on.

column2: the retail assembly of this very function, pasted in as the candidate, gets the identical DIFFERS (the first outside-memory event of the run differs before the function's own code matters), so the harness cannot compare it; the C was read against the assembly instruction for instruction (2026-10-18)

FlushCache is one syscall that writes back or invalidates the EE caches; the host has no caches to flush, so the port's C does nothing on purpose (libraries.tsv: "nothing to flush"), and C cannot make a syscall

hand-written register convention: retail takes the mesh in $t8, z in $v1, y in $v0, x in $at and returns the leaf word in $at (it leaves a row pointer in $v0), while the C takes them as arguments; fcheck reads the arguments from $a0-$a3 and compares only $v0, so neither the inputs nor the result line up (2026-10-18)

hand-written register convention: retail spins on the word $v1 points to (the callers leave a DMA channel's CHCR there, 0x1000D400), the C on its third argument; from a captured call the C reads whatever $a2 holds, so the run cannot compare (2026-10-18)

DMA hardware: retail starts the scratchpad-to-memory channel (writes 0x1000D480/D410/D420/D400) and returns the status in $v1 ($v0 keeps 0x100); the port's C copies the data itself and returns the status, and fcheck's interpreter neither runs the DMA nor compares $v1 (2026-10-18)

DMA hardware: retail stages the palette in the scratchpad with DMA (waits on 0x1000D400) and VU0; the C uses tables of its own, so only the scratchpad work area and the device accesses differ, the image written to main memory is the same (2026-10-18)
